name: elemental_carbon

phase_0.boundary_condition: The covalent network solid boundary where sp³ or sp² hybridized carbon atoms form a continuous lattice that contains all internal bonds and electronic states; the surface terminates dangling bonds or reconstructs to satisfy valence.

⊢.justification: A single carbon atom with four valence electrons before any bonding occurs; the void state prior to lattice formation.

⊣.justification: The completed periodic structure that encloses all internal bonds and electronic bands; the terminal anchor that contains the entire system.

≻.justification: Forward morphism: two carbon atoms approach and form a covalent sigma bond through orbital overlap, lowering energy toward the lattice ground state.

≺.justification: Reverse morphism: thermal or mechanical energy breaks a covalent bond, returning atoms to a higher-energy separated state; the descent transformation.

⋈.justification: Sequential chaining: each new bond extends the network by connecting to an existing atom, composing the local motif into the extended crystal.

⊙.justification: Identity/self-reference: the sp³, sp², or sp hybridization of a carbon atom recognizes itself through its local geometry and bond angles.

∈.justification: One carbon environment splits into competing nucleation pathways: diamond (sp³ tetrahedral) versus graphite (sp² planar) versus fullerene (curved sp²).

∋.justification: Rejoin: the competing nucleation arms recombine at a grain boundary or phase interface where multiple allotropes meet in a single sample.

⊤.justification: Affirmative arm: a covalent bond achieves its target length and angle, depositing constructive truth into the lattice register.

⊥.justification: Negative arm: orbital overlap is insufficient or geometry is strained, depositing constructive falsity — the bond does not form.

⊞.justification: Paradice: in graphite and aromatic systems, bonds are simultaneously single and double (resonance), holding both bond orders at once without resolution.

⊡.justification: Irreversible fixation: a Stone-Wales defect, vacancy, or dislocation is permanently recorded in the lattice; subsequent annealing cannot erase the topological record.

phase_3.void_description: Isolated carbon atom with unhybridized 2s²2p² valence configuration; no bonds, no lattice.
phase_3.true_description: A fully formed covalent bond at equilibrium length (1.54 Å sp³, 1.42 Å sp²) with correct tetrahedral or trigonal geometry.
phase_3.false_description: A failed bond attempt: atoms at wrong distance, wrong angle, or insufficient orbital overlap; the interaction does not lower energy.
phase_3.both_description: A resonant bond in graphite or benzene-like ring where bond order is 1.5 — simultaneously single and double, held without collapse to either Kekulé form.

steps.domain_action: Initialize with isolated carbon atom in vacuum — void state, no bonds, no lattice.
Carbon atom self-recognizes its four valence electrons and tetravalent nature.
First bond formation — two atoms approach, sp³ orbitals overlap, sigma bond forms.
Bond achieves target length 1.54 Å — affirmative deposit, stable sp³ connection.
Third atom bonds to the dimer — chain extends, lattice propagation begins.
Each new atom self-recognizes its hybridization state (sp³ for diamond path).
Fourth atom completes first tetrahedral unit — diamond motif established.
Tetrahedral angle 109.5° confirmed — second affirmative deposit.
Nucleation fork — system splits into diamond (sp³) and graphite (sp²) pathways.
Diamond arm — continued tetrahedral growth under high pressure.
Diamond arm — each new sp³ bond deposits affirmative truth.
Diamond arm — sequential lattice propagation in three dimensions.
Diamond arm — each atom self-recognizes tetrahedral coordination.
Graphite arm — reverse morphism from sp³ toward sp² planar geometry.
Graphite arm — sp³ bonds break (negative deposit), energy cost recorded.
Graphite arm — new sp² bonds form in planar hexagonal rings.
Graphite arm — sp² bonds at 1.42 Å deposit affirmative truth.
Graphite arm — resonant bonds form, holding single/double character simultaneously (B-state).
Graphite arm — sequential layer growth via van der Waals stacking.
Graphite arm — each atom self-recognizes trigonal planar coordination.
Phase coexistence — diamond and graphite arms rejoin at grain boundary, both coordinations present.
Grain boundary defect permanently recorded — irreversible topological record.
Continued growth from coexistence interface — new layers add to both phases.
New bonds on both sides of boundary deposit affirmative truth.
Second fork — fullerene nucleation pathway opens from graphite edge.
Fullerene arm — reverse morphism: planar sheet curves, pentagons introduce strain.
Fullerene arm — strain energy deposits negative (pentagon penalty).
Fullerene arm — curvature completes, cage closes (C60 or larger).
Fullerene arm — closed cage achieves stability, affirmative deposit.
Fullerene arm — conjugated π-system holds resonant bonds (B-state).
Fullerene rejoins graphite at nucleation site — three-phase junction.
Three-phase junction defect permanently recorded.
Continued lattice propagation from all three phases simultaneously.
Each atom in all phases self-recognizes its local coordination.
High-temperature annealing — bond rearrangement within phases.
Thermal desorption — surface bonds break, atoms leave lattice (reverse).
Desorption events deposit negative — bonds broken, not formed.
Surface reconstruction rejoins dangling bonds — partial healing.
Surface reconstruction pattern permanently recorded.
Infinite crystal lattice achieved — terminal anchor contains all phases, defects, boundaries.

phase_5.compiler_frontend: Quantum mechanical Hamiltonian (DFT/tight-binding) translating atomic positions into bond energies and electronic structure.
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Phonon-mediated lattice vibrations and electron-phonon coupling communicating strain and energy across the crystal.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: Topological defect registry (vacancies, dislocations, grain boundaries, Stone-Wales defects) stored in the lattice geometry itself.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: Thermodynamic driving force (Gibbs free energy minimization) and kinetic barriers (activation energies) determining which bond events occur and when.
phase_5.alfs_store: The periodic table entry for carbon (Z=6) and the Pauling covalent radius (0.76 Å) as the canonical bootstrap constants.

phase_6.cycle_cost: One covalent bond formation consumes ~3.6 eV (sp³) or ~7.4 eV (sp² resonance stabilized) of chemical potential; bond breaking requires equivalent thermal/mechanical input.
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: Disordered carbon vapor or amorphous carbon with high configurational entropy, unsatisfied valences.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: Ordered crystal lattice (diamond/graphite/fullerene) with low configurational entropy, all valences satisfied, defect registry fixed.
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The cycle conserves entropy because bond formation reduces configurational entropy but releases heat (phonons) that increases thermal entropy; the defect record (IFIX) stores the irreversible information loss as topological memory.

grounding_reasoning:
⊣=𐑡: Elemental carbon forms a covalent network solid with a connected graph structure.
⊢=𐑨: Elemental carbon forms extended crystalline structures (diamond, graphite) where constraints propagate through a 3D spatial lattice.
⊞=𐑙: Elemental carbon consists of identical atoms in a symmetric network where each carbon participates equivalently in covalent bonds with neighboring carbons.
⊡=𐑷: Elemental carbon's covalent network structure lacks topological protection and can be continuously deformed or transformed to other allotropes without crossing a topological boundary.
⊙=𐑢: Elemental carbon at standard conditions exists in stable allotropes (graphite, diamond) well away from critical points or phase transitions, operating in a normal subcritical regime.
⊥=𐑓: Elemental carbon allotropes (diamond, graphite, fullerenes) are achiral with mirror-image symmetry and no persistent broken orientational symmetry.
≻=𐑑: Elemental carbon interacts primarily through strong covalent bond formation and structural transformation between allotropes, which are irreversible or semi-reversible processes.
≺=𐑗: Elemental carbon forms non-polar covalent bonds between identical atoms with no directional preference or donor/acceptor distinction at the interface.
⋈=𐑐: Elemental carbon forms strong directional covalent bonds with specific geometries (sp³, sp²) that enforce near-certain interaction fidelity through orbital overlap.
⊤=𐑧: Elemental carbon allotropes (diamond, graphite) have extremely strong covalent bonds creating high kinetic barriers that require extreme temperature/pressure to overcome rearrangement.
∈=𐑔: Elemental carbon forms extended covalent network solids (diamond, graphite) where interactions propagate across the entire crystal lattice.
∋=𐑝: Elemental carbon in its network allotropes requires each atom to simultaneously engage with its specific nearest neighbors (3 or 4) to form the stable covalent lattice structure.
